meta.title: Nframa — Database Schema (Prisma-like JSON representation)
meta.queryLayer: This project uses Knex (query builder, no ORM) — see CLAUDE.md. This JSON is a planning/documentation artifact shaped like a Prisma schema for readability; it is not consumed by Prisma or any ORM.
meta.relationDirection: Relations are documented one-directionally from the foreign-key-owning field only (as a `relation` object on that field) — no reverse relation arrays — to keep this a compact reference rather than a full DMMF dump.
meta.polymorphicNote: A few columns point at different tables depending on a sibling discriminator column and are NOT real foreign keys — they carry `polymorphic: true` and a `possibleReferences` list instead of `relation`.

conventions.namingCase: camelCase for every table and column (e.g. walletTransactions.balanceAfterPesewas), matching the TypeScript codebase. Postgres folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase, so every identifier must be double-quoted — Knex's query builder does this automatically.
conventions.primaryKeys: uuid via gen_random_uuid() (pgcrypto, built into PG17) for nearly every table. Exceptions: platformSettings (fixed singleton, smallint id = 1), and the 1:1 profile tables (riderProfiles, carOwnerProfiles) which use userId itself as PK+FK.
conventions.displayCodes: Human-facing prefixed ids (e.g. TRP-7210, VER-5031) are never the primary key — each table that needs one has a separate `code text UNIQUE` column fed by a per-table Postgres sequence. APIs expose both `id` and `code`.
conventions.money: Integer pesewas (bigint), columns suffixed `Pesewas`. Exact arithmetic, no float drift; serialized to GHS decimal numbers only at the API layer.
conventions.timestamps: timestamptz everywhere; API responses are ISO 8601. Every table has createdAt/updatedAt unless noted otherwise on the model.
conventions.enums: Modeled here as named enum types for documentation clarity. Physically implemented as `text` + `CHECK` constraints per column, not native Postgres enums — adding a value is a migration-only constraint swap, not an ALTER TYPE.
conventions.softDelete: deletedAt (timestamptz, nullable) exists only on users, verificationApplications, supportTickets. Every other table is either immutable history (trips, ledger rows, audit logs, SOS alerts) or has no delete concept at all.
conventions.phoneNumbers: Always two columns, never one combined string: a `...CountryCode` column (numeric calling code, digits only, no `+`, e.g. "233") plus the number itself (national significant number only, no leading trunk `0`, e.g. "201234567"). Full E.164 is reconstructed at the API layer as `+${countryCode}${number}`. Applies to users.phoneCountryCode/phoneNumber and riderProfiles.emergencyContactCountryCode/emergencyContactPhone.
conventions.statusTransitions: Allowed status transitions (e.g. dispute open → underReview → resolved) are enforced in the service layer, not the database — the DB only stores the current status plus transition timestamps.

users.description: Shared identity for riders and car owners, keyed by phone. Role is not a column — it's the existence of a riderProfiles/carOwnerProfiles row.

fields.name: id
fields.note: used in QR payloads and JWT `sub`

fields.name: phoneNumber
fields.note: national significant number only, no leading 0 (e.g. "201234567")

derived.name: security.passwordChanged / loginLocation / devices
derived.description: admin UI's login-telemetry block — computed from authSessions, never stored on users

derived.name: tripsCompleted / averageRating
derived.description: aggregated from trips/ratings; denormalize onto this table later only if measured slow

fields.name: emergencyContactPhone
fields.note: nullable together with emergencyContactCountryCode — enforced at the service layer, not a DB CHECK

fields.name: verificationStatus
fields.note: denormalized from the latest verificationApplications row, kept in sync by the verification service

savedCommutes.description: A rider's saved default commute ("Home to Work"). Own table so multiple could coexist later.

partialUniqueIndexes.note: exactly one default commute per rider

vehicles.description: A car owner's vehicle. Separate table for photos + future multi-vehicle support.
notes: Vehicle photos live in `files` with purpose='vehiclePhoto' and ownerId = this vehicle's id.

suspensionCases.description: A user account suspension. Reinstating closes the case (reinstatedAt set) rather than deleting it, so history survives.

partialUniqueIndexes.note: at most one open case per user

adminUsers.description: Administration-console operators. A separate identity realm from users (email + password/OTP, not phone).
notes: A "Super Admin" cannot be suspended or deleted if it's the last one remaining — enforced in the service layer.

roles.description: Admin-creatable role definitions driving sidebar/module visibility.
notes: Deleting a role is blocked (FK RESTRICT / 409) while any adminUsers.roleId still references it.

derived.name: assigned admin count
derived.description: COUNT(*) over adminUsers grouped by roleId

otpCodes.description: One-time login/verification codes for phone (rider/driver) and email (admin) auth.

fields.name: identifier
fields.note: phone (phoneCountryCode+phoneNumber concatenated, no separators) or email

oneTimeTokens.description: Short-lived single-use tokens: admin forgot-password step-2 resetToken, future invite-activation links.

authSessions.description: Refresh-token sessions for both the user (rider/driver) and admin realms.
notes: Powers "revoke other sessions on password reset" and the admin UI's devices/loginLocation telemetry (see users.derived).

files.description: Generic upload registry (S3-style object storage; this table stores only the pointer, not bytes).

derived.name: fileUrl
derived.description: a signed, time-limited URL minted from storageKey at read time — never stored

routes.description: Admin-managed fixed corridors that trips run on.

fields.name: corridor
fields.note: grouping/filter label, e.g. "Accra–Tema" — see open question about promoting to its own table

derived.name: assignedCarOwners
derived.description: COUNT(*) over routeAssignments where unassignedAt IS NULL — never stored

routeAssignments.description: Which car owners currently serve which route.

partialUniqueIndexes.note: a car owner has at most one active assignment to a given route at a time

notes: Deleting a city referenced by routes.cityId is blocked (FK RESTRICT) — resolved open question, consistent with every other orphan-guard in the app.

fields.name: priority
fields.note: computed by a scheduled job (wait-time + document expiry proximity), never admin-set

notes: Business rule: any single document rejection ⇒ application status becomes 'rejected'.
Business rule: application becomes 'approved' only once ALL required documents are 'approved'.
A BullMQ sweep flips applications/documents to 'expiring'/'expiringSoon' as expiryDate approaches.

verificationDocuments.description: One row per submitted document VERSION — a resubmission inserts a new row pointing at the one it replaces.

fields.name: replacesDocumentId
fields.note: self-referencing; "current" doc per type = latest with no row referencing it

verificationEvents.description: Append-only timeline/activity log for a verification application.

fields.name: detail
fields.note: e.g. a sent-notification's full HTML body

schedules.description: A car owner's commute template — one-off or recurring (e.g. Mon–Fri). A background job materializes concrete trips from active schedules.
checkConstraints: exactly one of recurrenceDays / oneOffDate is set
notes: The 2-hour freeze rule (no cancel/edit within 2h of departure) is enforced in the service layer against trips.departureAt, not on this table.

trips.description: One concrete departure on a date. Route facts are snapshotted at creation so later route edits can't rewrite history.

fields.name: originName
fields.note: snapshot of route.originName at trip creation

fields.name: farePesewas
fields.note: per seat, snapshotted from route pricing

derived.name: seatsAvailable
derived.description: seatsTotal − SUM(confirmed booking seats), computed under a row lock at booking time — never stored

derived.name: "Disputed" badge (admin UI)
derived.description: derived as: status = completed AND an open tripDisputes row exists for this trip

bookings.description: One rider's seat reservation on a trip.

fields.name: qrToken
fields.note: random opaque server-issued token encoded in the boarding QR — NOT the guessable NFR-USERID-SCHEDULEID display format

boardingScans.description: Append-only log of every QR boarding scan attempt, including failed ones.

fields.name: bookingId
fields.note: NULL when the scan matched nothing

tripUpdateFailures.description: Telemetry/status-sync failures needing manual admin attention.

ratings.description: A trip-participant rating another participant after a completed trip.

misconductReports.description: A rider-filed misconduct report against a car owner. Governs a PERSON (behavior, account consequences) — see tripDisputes for trip-facts issues.

fields.name: category
fields.note: curated picklist in the app, stored as free text

notes: Status only moves forward: open → investigating → resolved OR dismissed (both terminal).

tripDisputes.description: A fare/route/damage dispute raised after a trip completes. Fixes a TRIP (money/facts) — see misconductReports for person-facing issues.
notes: Status moves open → underReview → resolved, or underReview → escalated → resolved. resolved is terminal.

walletAccounts.description: One row per (user, balance bucket) — models the four distinct rider/car-owner wallet balances.

fields.name: balancePesewas
fields.note: cache; authoritative value = SUM(walletTransactions.amountPesewas), reconciled by a job

derived.name: admin wallet status ("Payout ready"/"Restricted"/"Setup required")
derived.description: derived from user status, open suspensionCases, and presence of a payoutAccounts row — never stored

walletTransactions.description: Append-only ledger. Every money movement is a row here; nothing edits or deletes one — corrections are reversal entries.
notes: A completed trip settles as paired entries: rider tripPayment (−fare); owner ownerPending tripEarning (+fare) and commission (−fare × commission %); later a pendingRelease pair moves pending → available on the settlement cadence.
Admin wallet-page counts (payments, adjustments) are COUNT(*) grouped by type.

paymentMethods.description: A rider's funding sources (cards/MoMo). Only PSP tokens and masked display strings are stored — never raw PANs/full numbers.

partialUniqueIndexes.note: at most one default payment method per rider

payoutAccounts.description: A car owner's payout destination (Mobile Money or bank account).

transitPasses.description: A prepaid ride bundle ("14 of 20 rides left"). Product details (pricing tiers, expiry policy) are under-documented — see open questions.

fields.name: code
fields.note: display prefix not specified in source docs

withdrawalRequests.description: A car owner's payout request. Read-only for admins — decisions happen in payoutApprovals (segregation of duties).

payoutApprovals.description: The actual reviewer-decision record for a payout, hard-linked 1:1 to its withdrawalRequests row (unlike the frontend's unlinked mock fixtures).
notes: Only rows with outcome='awaitingApproval' AND eligibility='eligible' are decidable — enforced server-side, not just hidden in the UI.

refundRequests.description: A refund or service-credit request for a rider.
notes: "processed" vs "completed" distinction is ambiguous in the source docs — modeled as two stages (decision made vs money actually settled); confirm with product.

sosAlerts.description: Emergency SOS Desk incident. Never deleted — status transitions only.

fields.name: riderUserId
fields.note: the commuter; car-owner/vehicle details join through trip, not duplicated

notes: Status moves active → dispatched → resolved, or active → resolved directly. sosTimeoutMinutes auto-escalation is a delayed background job, not schema.

sosAlertNotes.description: Append-only operator call/verification log on an SOS alert.

supportTickets.description: A support ticket, either logged by an admin (phoned-in) or raised by a user in-app.

fields.name: reporterName
fields.note: snapshot — admin console can log a ticket for someone not yet linked to userId

notes: Replying to an open+unassigned ticket auto-transitions it to inProgress and auto-assigns the replying admin (service layer).

ticketReplies.description: One message in a support ticket's two-sided conversation thread.
checkConstraints: exactly one of authorAdminId / authorUserId is set, matching authorType

broadcasts.description: A notice composed and sent (or drafted) to riders/car owners via Broadcast Studio.

fields.name: message
fields.note: HTML for inApp/email; plain text for push (150 char) / sms (160 char), length validated server-side

notes: A 'sent' broadcast is permanent — no edit/delete once sent (409 CONFLICT), enforced server-side. Duplicating (any status, including sent) always creates a fresh 'draft' copy.

auditLogs.description: One append-only table serving three consumers: Administration Activity Logs, Finance Financial Audit Logs (module='finance'), and the Overview 'recent actions' feed. Written as a side effect of every consequential mutation.

fields.name: code
fields.note: prefix depends on consuming view — ACL- (Administration) or FAL- (Finance) — chosen by application logic, not a single DB sequence

platformSettings.description: Single-row table of platform-wide default configuration. routes carries its own baseFarePesewas/perKmRatePesewas which override these defaults per route.

settingsChangeLogs.description: Read-only diff-based trail of platform settings changes, written automatically on every settings update.

fields.name: changes
fields.note: [{ field, old, new }, ...] — diff-based, not one generic string

derivedNotStored: All Overview/stat-tile numbers, trends, donut breakdowns, cash-flow charts — aggregate queries (materialize/cache per-minute later if slow).
seatsAvailable on trips, assignedCarOwners on routes, permissionsCount on roles, per-role admin counts.
tripsCompleted, averageRating on users (aggregate over trips/ratings; denormalize only if measured slow).
Wallet display statuses (Payout ready / Restricted / Setup required), trip 'Disputed' badge, rider wallet Active/Suspended status.
The admin 'security' block (devices, loginLocation, passwordChanged) — from authSessions + users.
Filter-option lists (corridors, joined months, suspension reasons, …) — SELECT DISTINCT with indexes.
Wallet balances are cached on walletAccounts but the walletTransactions ledger is authoritative.
openQuestions: Hard vs soft delete for users / verification applications / tickets — this plan assumes soft delete + PII scrub.
Pesewas vs decimal GHS at the API boundary — this plan uses integer pesewas.
Transit pass product definition (pricing tiers, corridor scope, expiry policy) is under-documented.
Whether 'corridor' should become its own first-class table.
QR payload format — plan uses a server-issued random qrToken instead of the guessable NFR-USERID-SCHEDULEID display string.
Whether the same phone number is allowed to hold both a rider and a car-owner profile.
Trip materialization horizon for recurring schedules, and what happens to already-materialized trips on schedule edit.
Eligibility computation rules for payoutApprovals (policyReview / dutyConflict) are undefined in the source docs.
verificationApplications.priority computation formula is undefined; assumed job-computed from wait time + expiry proximity.
Whether phoneCountryCode is effectively fixed to Ghana ("233") at launch or must support other countries from day one.
